concept: At C the exterior angle and the interior angle next to it lie on a straight line, so together they make 180°.
The three interior angles also make 180°. Both pairs make 180° and share the angle at C, so the exterior angle equals the other two interior angles together.

workedExamples.prompt: One side of a triangle is extended. The two interior angles opposite the exterior angle are 39° and 112°. What is the exterior angle, in degrees?
familyExplainSteps: Exterior angle = sum of the interior opposite angles: 39° + 112° = 151°

workedExamples.prompt: One side of a triangle is extended. The exterior angle is 129° and one of the two interior opposite angles is 93°. What is the other interior opposite angle, in degrees?
lines: Interior angle next to the exterior angle C = 180° − 129° = 51° (straight line)

hints: Which interior angle sits next to the exterior angle, on the straight line?
That angle and the exterior angle make 180°; the three interior angles also make 180°.
So the exterior angle equals the two far interior angles added.
Which interior angle sits next to the exterior angle, on the straight line?
That angle and the exterior angle make 180°; the three interior angles also make 180°.
So the far angle is the exterior angle minus the other far angle.

alternativeExplanation.title: Go through the third angle
text: Find the third interior angle with the angle sum.
The exterior angle and that angle lie on a straight line, so the exterior angle is a straight angle minus the third angle.

whatWentWrong: In "One side of a triangle is extended. The two interior angles opposite the exterior angle are 34° and 27°. What is the exterior angle, in degrees?", one wrong answer is 119.
The third interior angle was found instead. The exterior angle sits outside, next to that angle, on the straight line.
The exterior angle is OUTSIDE the triangle, on the straight line next to the third angle; it is not the third angle.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check: the third angle is 119°; it and the exterior angle must make 180°, so the exterior angle is 61°.

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)

whatWentWrong: In "One side of a triangle is extended. The exterior angle is 135° and one of the two interior opposite angles is 108°. What is the other interior opposite angle, in degrees?", one wrong answer is 45.
The interior angle next to the exterior angle was found (180° − exterior). The question asks for the other opposite angle.
The question asks for an angle FAR from the exterior angle, not the one next to it.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check: 45° is the angle next to the exterior angle; the far angles add to 135°, so the other far angle is 27°.
solvedCorrectly: Interior angle next to the exterior angle C = 180° − 135° = 45° (straight line)

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)
misconceptions.note: the exterior angle used as a third interior angle

whatWentWrong: In "One side of a triangle is extended. The exterior angle is 128° and one of the two interior opposite angles is 45°. What is the other interior opposite angle, in degrees?", one wrong answer is 7.
The exterior angle was used as if it were inside the triangle (180° − 128° − 45°). The exterior angle equals the two opposite interior angles together.
The exterior angle is outside the triangle; it is not one of the three angles that make 180°.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check: 128° makes 180° with the interior angle next to it (52°). The interior angles are 45°, 52° and the one you want: 180° − 45° − 52° = 83°.
solvedCorrectly: Interior angle next to the exterior angle C = 180° − 128° = 52° (straight line)
